title: New Zealand women's suffrage
summary: On 19 September 1893 the Governor signed New Zealand's Electoral Act, giving adult women the right to vote in parliamentary elections, the first in a self-governing country. Women voted for the first time in the general election of 28 November 1893. Eligible women had to be British subjects, a category that included Māori women.

uncertainty.note: The Act passed the Legislative Council on 8 September 1893 and was signed on 19 September; the first vote followed on 28 November (20 December in the Māori electorates).

as_recorded.value: On 19 September 1893, Governor Lord Glasgow signed a new Electoral Act into law
Women first exercised their right to vote at the general election held on 28 November

where.historical_name: New Zealand, a self-governing British colony

importance.justification: First national electoral law to give women the vote in parliamentary elections, an early landmark in suffrage worldwide.
